newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn closes lower on exports, wheat/oil drop.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn closes lower on exports, wheat/oil drop.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed lower in quiet dealings with a lack of large-scale export sales of U.S. corn weighing on the market along with a drop in soyoil and wheat, traders said.
"Oil and wheat weighed on everything," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.
USDA Monday said during the week ended December 19, 40.8 million bushels of corn were inspected for export, below trade expectations for 42 million to 49 million bushels.
Traders said the markets remained quiet in a typical holiday mode. Markets close early at 1210 CST/1810 GMT Tuesday and remain closed Wednesday for the Christmas Day Holiday.
Friday's Commodity Futures Trading Commission Commitments of Traders report was about as expected, the traders said.
The CFTC said as of December 17, funds were long corn by 79.4 million bushels and short corn by 270.5 million bushels.

Traders said the corn market may have been underpinned by Friday's USDA Cattle on Feed report which showed the November placements at eight percent above a year ago. The trade was expecting a five percent increase.
Corn closed unchanged to 2-1/2 cents per bushel lower, with March down 1/4 at $2.66-1/2 a bushel.

Refco Inc sold 1.5 million bushels of March and Farmers Commodities Corp sold 1.5 million bushels of March, traders said. Iowa Grain bought 1.5 million May and Merrill Lynch Futures bought 1.5 million bushels of March, traders said.
Corn futures volume was estimated at 35,000 contracts, below the 46,817 traded Friday, according to the CBOT.
In corn options, Goldenberg Hehmeyer bought 500 July $3.90 calls and sold 500 July $3.70 calls at 1/4 cent, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 8,000 contracts, below the 12,106 traded Friday.
